17.0.s.en: (1) Elijah withholds the rain and the ravens feed him

17.0.0.en: Elijah: a name meaning "My God is Jehovah."

17.0.1.en: Ahab went to the furthest extent in the worship of idols. He was not content with the worship of the golden calves that Jeroboam had made, but worshiped Baal abundantly, to the degree that he had 850 prophets of Baal and of the groves. His pagan wife Jezebel helped and encouraged him in that, so he was in truth the most wicked of the kings of Israel, and by this he drew his people away from the worship of God. So God was compelled to discipline them in deed and not by mere warning, and the prophet Elijah appeared, after Ahab had killed the prophets of God and the rest had hidden for fear of him. Obadiah, who worked with the king, had hidden some of them and was feeding them. Elijah was one of the dwellers of the village of Tishbe in the region of Gilead, lying east of the Jordan, where there are many wildernesses, so he lived as an ascetic man who spent most of his life in the wilderness, which helped him to be courageous and to have a strong relationship with God, for he felt the presence of God, which kept him far from sin and gave him boldness in his service. The Holy Bible does not mention his father or his clan, so that some of the Jews thought that he was an angel, but the Apostle James affirms that he was a man like us (Jas 5:17). He was an apostle from God to proclaim His voice among the wicked people, like John the Baptist, who also lived in the wilderness and then appeared to prepare the way of Christ.

17.0.2.en: Elijah stood among the people before the wicked King Ahab in his capital Samaria and announced God's discipline of the whole people, for he commanded the heavens not to rain or give dew, and it continued for three years and six months (Jas 5:17), and this means:

17.0.3.en: 1- A community in the whole land.

17.0.4.en: 2- The authority of the children of God over nature.

17.0.5.en: This divine discipline shows the helplessness of the pagan gods on whom Ahab relied, chief among them Baal, for they could not lift the famine even if Ahab claimed that they were the source of goodness and fertility. Thus God brought them into an affliction unto death by hunger, that perhaps they would repent and return to Him.

17.0.6.en: It is understood from the epistle of James that Elijah prayed and then commanded the heavens and they obeyed him, so by prayer he drew on the power of God, who is able to do all things.

17.0.7.en: Elijah's saying "As the Lord lives, before whom I stand" means the following:

17.0.8.en: 1- That God is living, while the idols have no life in them.

17.0.9.en: 2- Elijah's constant feeling that he is before God, and this gives him fear of God, purity and strength.

17.0.10.en: Do not be afraid to proclaim the voice of God however much the obstinate stand before you, but be concerned to pray first, so that the words may be from God and you may keep your humility when you speak.

17.1.0.en: The brook Cherith: a watercourse opposite the Jordan that flows into it from the east.

17.1.1.en: It was the divine plan that Elijah should hide so that the king would not know his place until the period of discipline ended, in order to give the people an opportunity to repent. So the Lord asked him to leave Samaria and go east of the Jordan to hide by the brook Cherith, which is opposite the Jordan. In the midst of the drought God provided him water from the stream of the brook Cherith and sent him food by the ravens.

17.1.2.en: Thus Elijah went far from Ahab and walked a long distance from Samaria and crossed the Jordan to live in the wilderness and complete his solitude and his worship of God. There, when the famine came and spread over all the land of the children of Israel, God did not forget His prophet Elijah, but sent the ravens to feed him. We notice several things in the ravens' feeding of Elijah:

17.1.3.en: 1- God's authority over the birds: He turns the birds that snatch food from men into birds that bring it to them.

17.1.4.en: 2- Ravens fear man, but here they approach quietly and serve him because God commanded them to do so.

17.1.5.en: 3- From where did the ravens bring this delicious, prepared food! Only from God.

17.1.6.en: 4- Ravens were among the unclean birds for the Jews, as the Law prescribes, but God turns them to the service of men, to declare that He is the Lord of the Law, who uses it or changes it according to the need of His children, and that the birds are clean in His sight, as will appear in the New Testament; in the Old Testament, however, He taught them some spiritual teachings, as a transitional stage to the New Testament, the covenant of grace.

17.1.7.en: 5- The regularity of the ravens' coming at fixed times for many days declares God's perfect care for His children.

17.1.8.en: If God turned the unclean raven into a servant of His prophet, He is able to turn you, however great your evil, into a clean person, and even a servant in the Church, to care for His children.

17.2.0.en: Elijah obeyed the word of God and went to the brook Cherith, and there he experienced the love of God and His care. He drank from the brook and the ravens fed him twice a day, morning and evening, with delicious food of bread and meat. It was delicious food because it was from God, so in his solitude he enjoyed God's care more than the prophets of Baal enjoyed the table of Jezebel, filled with luxurious foods every day (ch. 18:19). Thus God provided for Elijah with water from a small brook, Cherith, and not the great river Jordan, for God can care for the needs of His children even from small sources, as He afterward fed him by means of a poor widow.

17.2.1.en: Elijah lived in seclusion with God at the brook, and for most of the days of his life, so he had an opportunity for prayer and contemplation and a strong relationship with God, which helped him to stand courageously before the wicked King Ahab.

17.2.2.en: In proportion to your concern for your prayers, your readings and your meditations on the word of God, you are able to face the problems of life, serve God and proclaim His voice, whatever afflictions you meet, because God will support you and work through you, and you will always be strong.

17.3.0.en: It came to pass after a period of time that the brook dried up, because the heavens had not rained at all during this period.

17.4.s.en: (2) The widow of Zarephath of Sidon feeds Elijah

17.4.0.en: Zarephath: a small village lying on the Mediterranean Sea south of the city of Sidon, eight miles from it, on the road to Tyre.

17.4.1.en: After the famine increased because the waters of the rivers dried up, God commanded Elijah to leave the brook Cherith, which lies near his homeland Gilead east of the Jordan, and go to the village of Zarephath of Sidon, so he crossed the river Jordan and headed toward the Mediterranean Sea. This shows:

17.4.2.en: 1- That God is able to provide for His prophet near his homeland, or in any country far from it, that is, in every place.

17.4.3.en: 2- It also shows Elijah's obedience to God, for he went to the homeland of the wicked Jezebel, the daughter of the king of Sidon, and was not afraid of her violence, because God is able to protect him.

17.4.4.en: 3- Likewise God declares that He is the God of all peoples, so He used the Gentiles to provide for His prophet, as He used the Jews.

17.4.5.en: 4- There can be believers among the Gentiles better than all the people of the Jews who worshiped Baal; the woman of Zarephath of Sidon believed the word of the man of God Elijah, so God chose her out of all the women of the children of Israel to feed Elijah in the famine (Lk 4:26), for she was better in her faith than all the Jewish women.

17.4.6.en: 5- God did not send Elijah to a king or a great ruler, but to a poor widow to feed him, because it is God who provides through men, for they are instruments in His hand.

17.4.7.en: This widow is a type of the Church, which is in an appearance of weakness, but God works in her because of her faith in Him, and she gathers the Gentiles as well as the Jews.

17.4.8.en: Elijah is a type of Christ, who goes to the Gentiles and asks them for His needs and blesses them, as Christ went to the Samaritan woman and asked her for water, and preached in Galilee of the Gentiles because His own rejected Him, as the people of God rejected Elijah and worshiped Baal (Jn 4).

17.5.0.en: At the entrance of the city he saw a woman gathering sticks, so he turned to her and asked her for a little water in a vessel to drink.

17.6.0.en: A morsel of bread: any kind of food, even a little. As she was going to fetch him water, as he had asked, he called to her, saying: Bring me, I pray thee, a morsel of bread in thine hand.

17.7.0.en: The barrel: a vessel in which flour is kept.

17.7.1.en: As the Lord thy God liveth: This Gentile widow had probably learned that Elijah was a Jew, or a prophet, from his language or his clothing, so she believed in his God that He is a great God, even though she had not rejected her pagan gods. The famine had spread to Tyre and Sidon, so the woman told him that she had no cake, or any bread, or food, but all she had was a little flour in a vessel and a little oil in a cruse, and that she was gathering a few sticks to cook on her fire, to make for herself and her son what they might eat, and thus what she had of food would be finished, and she and her son would be exposed to death by hunger.

17.7.2.en: The widow's words were a statement of the facts and not a complaint or grumbling, for she was calm, as is proved by her faith in the God of Elijah, which would appear in her obedience to his word and her great generosity, for she would give him out of her want, that is, the little she had, despite the spread of the famine.

17.7.3.en: Thus, as Abraham was a cause of blessing to all the earth, the wicked Ahab was a cause of curse and of the spread of famine in his land and in all the lands around him.

17.7.4.en: In proportion as you please God, He blesses your life and blesses those around you, and they love you for the sake of the blessing of God that has come upon them because of your being with them. Be confident in your God and rely on Him, for He keeps you, satisfies you and blesses you in every place.

17.8.0.en: Elijah reassured her and told her not to fear anything, and asked her to prepare for herself and her son what she had resolved, on condition that she first make him a little cake and bring it to him, and afterward make for herself and her son.

17.8.1.en: We ought to put God first, giving the firstfruits and the tithes, and trust that the blessing of God will bless the rest, so that it suffices and overflows, however difficult our material circumstances.

17.9.0.en: In the spirit of prophecy Elijah gave her a promise from God that the barrel of flour would not be emptied nor the cruse of oil fail until the drought ended and the rain fell. Thus we find Elijah witnessing for God and working a miracle among the Gentiles, and even near the homeland of Queen Jezebel, the wicked daughter of the king of Sidon, and this shows his courage and faithfulness in his service.

17.10.0.en: The woman did not doubt for a moment what Elijah had told her, and she relied on the promise of God and on the generosity and love of giving that characterized her, so she went and did as the prophet had told her, and food was supplied to her, so that she and her son ate for a long time, without the barrel of flour being emptied or the cruse of oil failing, exactly as the Lord had said by the mouth of Elijah. These days were about two years, that is, until the end of the famine.

17.10.1.en: Thus we see that the woman's giving out of her want made her receive a blessing and generous giving from God, which satisfied her and her son throughout the famine, and perhaps she also invited her relatives to eat with her, so that she was by this a preacher of God among her Gentile relatives.

17.11.s.en: (3) Elijah raises the widow's son from the dead

17.11.0.en: After those events her only son was struck by a sudden illness, and the severity of the illness increased moment by moment until he died.

17.12.0.en: When the widow's son died she did not grumble, but this led her to repentance. For if the famine had come upon the earth and the rain had not fallen because of the sins of men, then the death of her son could be because of her sins. She felt that Elijah was a prophet, so she called him a man of God, and she also felt that he was righteous and she a sinner, not worthy of his presence in her house, so she confessed that she was a sinner and that the death of her son was a reminder to her of her sins so that she might repent. Thus we see how this widow was distinguished in her faith and repentance above all the people of God, for God sent Elijah to this woman and not to any other woman of the children of Israel, and worked this miracle of blessing the oil and the flour in her house, because of her distinction in faith in God. Although she was a Gentile, her repentance preceded the repentance of the people of God, for Ahab was still persisting in evil and the people of Israel were following him.

17.13.0.en: Elijah asked her to give him her son, so he took him from her arms and carried him up into a chamber on the roof, where he was staying, and laid the child on his bed. We understand from this the generosity of the widow, for she had given him a separate chamber on the roof in which to live in his freedom and continue his worship of God. We also see the faith of Elijah, who was not troubled by the death of the widow's son, but carried him in faith to the upper room and laid him on his bed to pray there, confident of God's power to raise this boy. Although he had not heard of a dead person being raised before this, he believed in the power of God, and perhaps the Holy Spirit guided him and encouraged him to pray that he might raise the boy from death.

17.13.1.en: Do not be troubled if adverse things or severe trials happen in your life, but take refuge in God by prayer and be confident that He will hear you and will not leave you.

17.14.0.en: Elijah prayed to God, reproaching Him with boldness, and said to Him: why have You done evil to this woman by killing her son, when she is a woman great in her faith, her obedience, her generosity, and then her repentance? Elijah was not troubled; on the contrary he spoke with boldness, confident that God hears him and will intervene.

17.15.0.en: The prophet stretched himself upon the child three times and cried out, calling upon the Lord, praying to Him, entreating that the soul of this child might come into him again.

17.15.1.en: He stretched himself upon him because he believed in the power of God that was in him and in God's ability to transfer this power to the boy so that he would live. He stretched himself three times in the name of the Holy Trinity, who is able to do all things, and his stretching himself three times also shows his perseverance in prayer.

17.15.2.en: From here we see the importance of the blessing of the saints and of touching anything connected with them, such as their relics, or the incense placed upon them on their feast days, for the blessing is a grace with which God distinguishes His children, so that they become a blessing to all around them. God supported Elijah with extraordinary miracles, for he was the first to bless food so that it became abundant and the first to raise a dead person, though he differs from Christ in that he prayed and the dead person rose, whereas Christ commanded with authority and then the dead person rose. All this divine support was because evil had spread intensely in the days of Elijah and most of the people of God had worshiped idols and there was no one to witness for God, so Elijah witnessed for Him with powerful miracles, he and Elisha after him.

17.16.0.en: The Lord heard the prayer of Elijah, and the soul of the child came into him again, and he lived.

17.16.1.en: Thus the affliction turned into a blessing; that is, the death of the boy was a blessing in the working of a great miracle for the first time in the history of mankind, namely the raising of a dead person, just as the want of bread in the widow's house turned into a blessing that never ended.

17.17.0.en: Elijah took the child and brought him down from the roof of the house into the house and delivered him to his mother, saying: See, thy son liveth.

17.17.1.en: Since it was a surprise to the woman to see her son standing on his feet, Elijah alerted her and encouraged her to rejoice and believe that her son had regained life.

17.18.0.en: Before this miracle that was accomplished by the hands of Elijah, the woman was certain that he was a man of God and that what he uttered of the words of the Lord was true, and she declared her faith in God.

17.18.1.en: The acceptance of Elijah's sacrifice and the killing of the prophets of Baal
